Step Four of Nine

Where the planning step sits when you're preparing ahead for Mom's care.

Download PDF

You've read about care, about finances, about Medicaid, and it's hard to tell how the pieces connect or which one your family is on. They connect in an order, and when there's time you can take them one at a time.

This page shows the nine steps, where the planning step sits among them, what it draws on, and who is involved after it.

Phase 1 · Assess

Understand where you are today.

  1. 1

    Understand Care Needs → Levels of Care & Costs → Care Plan

    You finish with: Future Care Planning Assessment

  2. 2

    Organize Income & Assets → Ownership & Expenses → Financial File

    You finish with: Family Financial Inventory

  3. 3

    Assess Care & Nonfinancial Eligibility → Income & Assets → Barriers & Readiness

    You finish with: Medicaid Readiness Assessment

Phase 2 · Plan

Develop and implement your strategy.

  1. 4

    Plan Barriers & Issues → Priorities & Professional Team → Written Plan

    You finish with: Advance Medicaid Planning Roadmap

    You are here. This is the step where the first three come together. What you've learned about Mom's care needs, the financial picture you've organized and where things stand with Medicaid are brought into one written plan showing what can be done now, what should be monitored, and what events would trigger action.

  2. 5

    Legal Authority & Documents → Property, Trusts & Transfers → Attorney Review

    You finish with: Legal Planning Review

  3. 6

    Financial Costs & Runway → Asset Treatment & Tools → Strategy & Documentation

    You finish with: Long-Term Care Funding Plan

Phase 3 · Secure

Secure benefits, protect assets, and maintain eligibility.

  1. 7

    Apply Prepare → Submit → Manage

    You finish with: Medicaid Application-Ready File

  2. 8

    Protect What May Be Protected → What May Remain Exposed → What Needs Ongoing Attention

    You finish with: Asset Protection Assessment

  3. 9

    Maintain Ongoing Requirements → Changes & Renewals → Maintenance System

    You finish with: Medicaid Monitoring & Maintenance System

What this step draws on

The three steps before it: a picture of the care Mom needs and wants, her finances gathered into one file, and a look at where things stand with Medicaid. A family planning ahead often arrives with some of these half done. That's ordinary, and bringing the pieces together is how you see which ones are thin.

What this step produces

A written long-term-care and Medicaid plan for your family: what can be done now, what should be monitored, and what events would trigger action. It is built in the course with your Medicaid planner, moving from the issues to look at, to priorities and the professional team, to the written plan. A page like this one doesn't produce it, and neither do a family's notes.

What happens next

Two steps finish this phase, Legal and Financial, and each belongs to a licensed professional. The Administration for Community Living describes an elder law attorney's work as helping create a legal framework so that a person's medical and financial wishes are fulfilled. The planning step is what gets a family ready for those conversations.1

The third phase begins with an application, if one is ever made. Whether a person is eligible is the state's to decide: the Administration for Community Living explains that the states operate Medicaid day to day, including taking applications and making determinations of eligibility. For a family planning ahead, the written plan is reviewed on a schedule in the meantime.2

Who is involved, by role

  • You and your family: gathering, writing down, noticing, and talking over who takes part.
  • Mom: what she wants, in her own words.
  • Your Medicaid planner: brings the family's care needs, preferences, finances, Medicaid-readiness findings and existing legal planning into one picture, helps separate what can be addressed now from what should be monitored, and names the events that should trigger action.
  • An elder law attorney: reviews the legal issues.
  • A licensed financial professional and a licensed insurance professional: review the issues that belong to them.

What this page doesn't promise

How long any step takes, who will be available, or how things turn out. It doesn't say Mom will need Medicaid or would qualify for it. Families planning ahead move through the steps at their own pace. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.
